target_customer: Urban consumers, about 70 percent women, sending flowers and gifts, plus some corporate buyers
problem: Ordering flowers from wire services was slow and pricey; BloomThat offered curated bouquets from about $38 delivered on demand.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer on-demand flower and gift delivery with local florist and courier partners

founders.name: Matthew Schwab
founders.background_notes: Background before BloomThat not found in sources opened.

investors: A-Grade Investments (Ashton Kutcher and Guy Oseary)

competitors.name: FTD
competitors.what: Established flower retailer and wire service
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent; founder said it was slow to adapt to on-demand phone ordering

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering app and dispatch to couriers and local florists; the difficulty was operational logistics rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Flowers via local florists and couriers were easy to copy; the brand and speed were the main edge, and big players could add same-day service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: FTD reportedly bought BloomThat for a small amount in January 2018 and the on-demand service was paused later that year.

market_need_then: In 2013 the founder cited an $8 billion national cut-flower market (unverified) and said incumbents were not adapting to phone ordering; revenue grew tenfold in three months and 40 percent of customers reordered within 60 days.

branding.domain_note: bloomthat.com; did not resolve in this session.

identity.visual_style: Branded burlap sack and card packaging per TechCrunch 2013
identity.voice_and_tone: Fun and approachable, built on delivering happiness

branding.brand_signature: Bouquets delivered in a branded burlap sack
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage framed it as Uber for flowers and drew celebrity investors such as Ashton Kutcher, which helped press.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct packaging and Uber-for-flowers press plus celebrity backers, but no sourced evidence of a mascot or community beyond launch coverage.

pivots.to: Flowers plus gifts and next-day delivery across California
pivots.why: TechCrunch June 2015 described growth beyond flower delivery to gifts

outcome_analysis: BloomThat grew quickly in 2013 to 2015 with about 500 orders per day in the Bay Area and raised $7.5 million in total, but flowers were easy to copy and big incumbents and other startups such as UrbanStems competed. FTD reportedly bought it for a small sum in January 2018 and the on-demand service was paused in September 2018. Sources do not state the cause, so the failure factors are a judgment from a modest sale, with 2015 unit economics said to be positive.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch and Seedtable ($2M, February 2014). June 2015 round of $5.5M stage not stated by TechCrunch so labelled other, aggregators call it Series A. TechCrunch 2018 says $7.5M total, consistent with these rounds, and says the acquisition was reportedly completed (via Axios) with a small price. TechCrunch 2018 says the most recent round was April 2015 while the round article is dated June 16, 2015, a small conflict. bloomthat.com did not resolve in this session. Founder education not found. Failure factors are a judgment, not stated by sources.
